title: Linear-space Cutting Planes refutations
formal:
Does there exist one constant \(C\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\) such that every unsatisfiable CNF formula on \(n\) Boolean variables has a Cutting Planes refutation using total space at most \(C(n+1)\), with the exact rules and space measure below?
\[
\exists C\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ \forall n\in\mathbb N_0\
\forall F\in\operatorname{CNF}_n\
\left(\operatorname{Unsat}(F)\ \Longrightarrow\
\exists\Pi\
\left[\operatorname{Ref}_{\mathrm{CP}}(F,\Pi)
\land\operatorname{TotSp}(\Pi)\le C(n+1)\right]\right).
\]
Here \(n\) counts variables, rather than clauses, literal occurrences or the binary length of the whole input. There is no restriction on the number of clauses, proof length or coefficient magnitudes. The same constant \(C\) must work for every \(n\) and \(F\); the finite refutation \(\Pi\) may depend on \(F\). The \(n+1\) convention includes formulas with no variables and is equivalent to the source's asymptotic linear bound.

source_formulation.text: Can every unsatisfiable CNF be refuted in CP in linear total space?
source_formulation.caption: Complete selected source sentence; PDF p. 14

why: The question tests a basic memory limit of a central arithmetic proof system used to study pseudo-Boolean reasoning. Counting only inequalities hides the cost of large coefficients, whereas total space records that cost. A resolution would determine whether the known constant-line-space phenomenon extends to a linear numerical representation budget, or whether some Boolean contradictions force additional simultaneous information even when arbitrarily long proofs are permitted. This is a universal structural question about the proof system, with a separate meaning from lower bounds on proof length.
status_note: Open as stated in CCC 2015, Section 7, Problem 2. A bounded later-source review through 16 September 2026 found no verified resolution. The 2021 handbook account still describes a linear-versus-quadratic total-space gap; inspected 2020/2021 length-space and coefficient tradeoffs, the November 2024 size-depth result, and the July 2026 clique proof-length result do not settle the unrestricted-length total-space target. This is not an exhaustive literature review, an independent verification of the cited proofs, or a Lean verification. The apparent linear-space claim in Corollary 6 of an older 29 October 2014 author draft conflicts with its own introduction and is corrected to quadratic space in the final 2015 proceedings; it is not treated as a resolution.

importance.reason: Individual assessment: this asks for the universal memory capacity of Cutting Planes once integer magnitudes are charged, bridging a sharp constant-line-space phenomenon and a persistent linear-versus-quadratic total-space gap. Its scope is an entire established proof system, and it distinguishes arithmetic compression from genuine simultaneous storage. The score reflects this foundational breadth and relevance to proof complexity, rather than merely the presence of an open-problem paragraph; it replaces the explicitly unassessed midpoint 50.

sentences: Cutting Planes refutes a Boolean CNF by deriving integer linear inequalities until it obtains a contradiction.
Total space counts the binary digits of coefficients and right-hand constants stored simultaneously, with the source's convention that variable names and signs are not charged.
The question is whether one constant times the number of variables always suffices, with no limit on proof length or coefficient magnitude.
The source gives a quadratic universal upper bound, and the bounded later-source review found no resolution of the remaining linear-space question.
An accepted answer must prove the universal linear bound or its fully quantified failure in Lean for the exact rules and space measure stated here.

definitions:
Put \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \([0]=\varnothing\), and let the variables be \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\). A clause is a pair of subsets \(P,N\subseteq[n]\), representing the disjunction of the positive literals \(x_i\), \(i\in P\), and negative literals \(\neg x_i\), \(i\in N\). Repeated occurrences of a literal are removed. A CNF \(F\in\operatorname{CNF}_n\) is a finite set of such clauses, interpreted as their conjunction; tautological clauses are allowed. A valuation is a map \(v:[n]\to\{0,1\}\). It satisfies \((P,N)\) exactly when some \(i\in P\) has \(v(i)=1\), or some \(i\in N\) has \(v(i)=0\). Thus
\[
\operatorname{Unsat}(F)\ \Longleftrightarrow\
\forall v:[n]\to\{0,1\}\ \exists(P,N)\in F\
\left[(\forall i\in P,\ v(i)=0)\land
(\forall i\in N,\ v(i)=1)\right].
\]
The empty clause is false and the empty conjunction is true. Allowing unused variables in \([n]\) does not change the universal assertion, since one can also take \(n\) to be the number of variables that occur and rename them.

A line is a pair \(J=(a,b)\), where \(a\in\mathbb Z^n\) and \(b\in\mathbb Z\), denoting \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\ge b\). Terms are collected, zero coefficients are omitted, and the constant is on the right. Equality of lines means equality of these integer data, not logical equivalence. There are no extension variables, semantic inference rules or implicit rescaling operations.

The input line for clause \((P,N)\) is
\[
\sum_{i\in P}x_i-\sum_{i\in N}x_i\ge 1-|N|.
\]
Let \(A(F)\) be the set of these lines after collecting coefficients. Besides downloading a line in \(A(F)\), the permitted rules are exactly the following.

1. For each \(i\in[n]\), introduce either Boolean axiom \(x_i\ge0\) or \(-x_i\ge-1\).
2. Choose any integer \(k\ge1\), currently stored lines \((a^{(1)},b_1),\ldots,(a^{(k)},b_k)\), and positive integers \(s_1,\ldots,s_k\), and derive
\[
\left(\sum_{j=1}^k s_j a^{(j)},\ \sum_{j=1}^k s_j b_j\right).
\]
There is no fixed upper bound on the number \(k\) of premises. A premise may be selected more than once, equivalently by increasing its multiplier.
3. From a currently stored line \((a,b)\), choose an integer \(d\ge1\) dividing every \(a_i\), and derive
\[
\left(a/d,\ \left\lceil b/d\right\rceil\right).
\]
Division of \(a\) is coordinatewise. The ceiling is the least integer greater than or equal to the rational number \(b/d\), also when \(b\) is negative.

A memory configuration \(M\) is a finite set of lines. A refutation \(\Pi=(M_0,\ldots,M_T)\) is a finite sequence, with \(T\in\mathbb N_0\), starting with \(M_0=\varnothing\) and ending with \((0,1)\in M_T\), the contradiction \(0\ge1\). At each step, either \(M_{t+1}=M_t\cup\{J\}\), where \(J\in A(F)\), \(J\) is a Boolean axiom, or \(J\) follows by one permitted rule using premises in \(M_t\); or \(M_{t+1}\subsetneq M_t\), an erasure. This defines \(\operatorname{Ref}_{\mathrm{CP}}(F,\Pi)\). In particular, premises and a new conclusion coexist before a later erasure; overwriting a premise is not a free operation. An erased input line may be downloaded again. The full input need never be present simultaneously.

For \(z\in\mathbb Z\), let its unsigned binary length be
\[
\beta(z)=
\begin{cases}
1,&z=0,\\
1+\lfloor\log_2|z|\rfloor,&z\ne0.
\end{cases}
\]
This uses the one-digit representation of zero and omits leading zeroes. Define
\[
\operatorname{size}(a,b)=\beta(b)+
\sum_{\substack{i\in[n]\\a_i\ne0}}\beta(a_i),\qquad
\operatorname{sp}(M)=\sum_{J\in M}\operatorname{size}(J),\qquad
\operatorname{TotSp}(\Pi)=\max_{0\le t\le T}\operatorname{sp}(M_t).
\]
This is the source's numerical-symbol measure: count binary digits of nonzero coefficients and the right-hand constant, ignoring signs, variable names or indices, punctuation and arithmetic symbols. It is not the bit length of a fully serialized proof or machine memory. The conceptual vector \(a\) does not charge for its zero entries. Each distinct stored line is counted once. Input lines count while stored; the separate input, previous erased lines, proof history and rule annotations or multipliers do not count. There is no running-time, randomization or effective proof-search requirement: the target concerns existence of finite syntactically valid refutations.
answer_criterion:
Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the displayed assertion or of its full negation, using exactly the CNF encoding, inference rules, configurations and total-space measure above.

A positive answer must establish a single universal constant \(C\ge1\) and a finite refutation meeting \(C(n+1)\) for every unsatisfiable \(F\in\operatorname{CNF}_n\). No uniform polynomial-time procedure for finding the refutations is required.

A negative answer must prove
\[
\forall C\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ \exists n\in\mathbb N_0\
\exists F\in\operatorname{CNF}_n\
\left(\operatorname{Unsat}(F)\land
\forall\Pi\
\left[\operatorname{Ref}_{\mathrm{CP}}(F,\Pi)
\Longrightarrow
\operatorname{TotSp}(\Pi)>C(n+1)\right]\right).
\]
The final universal quantifier includes proofs of every finite length and every integer coefficient magnitude. The counterexample formula may depend on \(C\); a fixed power-law lower bound is not required. A bound only for short proofs, bounded coefficients, a restricted inference system or a different space measure does not establish this negation. This is an asymptotic existence question with a constant-factor linear bound, so the numerical \(1/100\) tolerance does not replace its quantifiers or inequalities.

context_blocks.text: Galesi, Pudlák and Thapen's 2015 Problem 2 asks precisely whether every unsatisfiable CNF has a Cutting Planes refutation in linear total space. Their parameter is the number of variables, and their Section 2 ignores variable-name length while charging coefficient magnitudes in binary.

The same paper proves that five simultaneously stored inequalities suffice without coefficient restrictions, and gives an \(O(n^2)\) total-space upper bound. The former result counts lines, so it does not already give the linear total-space conclusion.

Buss and Nordström's 2021 handbook chapter records a linear lower bound and a quadratic general upper bound for total space, with no known superlinear lower bound at the time of that account. These are dated statements, not a claim that all later literature has been exhausted.

The later papers checked here establish length-space tradeoffs, a bounded-coefficient length-space separation, size-depth tradeoffs, and a 2026 proof-length lower bound. Their resource restrictions differ from this card's unrestricted-length total-space question, and none of their inspected statements settles it.

Read the actual CCC2015 publisher PDF, especially Section 2 printed pp. 436–437/PDF4–5, Introduction pp. 434–435, Corollary 4.1 printed p. 441/PDF9, and Section 7 printed p. 446/PDF14. Problem 2 asks about every unsatisfiable CNF in linear total space; n is the number of variables. The input CNF can have arbitrarily many clauses, including exponentially many in n. Neither proof length nor effective proof search is part of the target.

The final source permits a single inference to form a positive-integer combination of arbitrarily many simultaneously stored premises. Footnote 2 explicitly warns that a binary-addition/unary-multiplication presentation may change other complexity measures even though inequality space agrees. The draft therefore retains the source's arbitrary-fan-in rule instead of asserting an unproved constant-factor total-space equivalence between the two presentations. Repeating a premise in a combination is absorbed in its positive multiplier and needs no duplicate set entry.

Section 2 defines total space using all nonzero coefficient binary lengths and the constant term, ignoring signs. Footnote 3 deliberately ignores variable names; charging binary indices may add a logarithmic factor. The draft does not identify this measure with full machine bit space. Taking zero to occupy one binary digit makes the RHS-zero case explicit; it is the usual encoding completion and has no asymptotic effect. Coefficients are canonically collected and constants moved right before charging; no multiplication or gcd reduction is a free normalization.

The proof model uses finite sets of inequalities. A new conclusion is added to the current set while its premises remain present, and erasure is a separate move. Input axioms can be downloaded repeatedly. Fixed original variables, syntactic integer rules, and no extension or semantic inference are specified. The target is proof existence, so no probabilistic computation model or polynomial verification/search budget is imposed. The n+1 convention and zero-variable formulas are an explicit asymptotic edge convention.

The final proceedings give O(n^2) total space, not O(n), in Corollary 4.1 on printed p. 441. The older author-hosted CP_constant_space.pdf has the title date 29 October 2014; its Corollary 6 printed p. 10 says O(n), but its introduction printed p. 3 says O(n^2), and the final proceedings correct the corollary to O(n^2). Read together these are an internal typo in the old draft, not a later resolution. Search-engine freshness metadata for that static PDF must not be read as a 2025 result.

Read the author-hosted Buss–Nordstrom 2021 handbook chapter preprint, especially its own p. 72: it records linear total-space lower bounds and quadratic general upper bounds, with no known superlinear total-space lower bounds. Its separate numbered Open Problem 7.15 concerns bounded-coefficient line space. Pages 74–75 distinguish coefficient-restricted and length-space tradeoffs. The obsolete KTH copy failed to download; the current author-domain PDF was cached and actually read. Its local preprint pagination is not the published chapter pagination.

Read de Rezende–Nordstrom–Vinyals ECCC TR21-006, 18 January 2021, Section 1.2 Theorems 1.1–1.2 pp. 3–4 and Section 2.1 p. 7. These bound proof length as a function of small line space, while exhibiting small-total-space upper bounds for the same special formulas. They do not show that those formulas require superlinear total space when proof length is unlimited. Their binary inference presentation is separately recorded and not silently substituted into the original 2015 total-space question.

Read de Rezende–Meir–Nordstrom–Pitassi–Robere–Vinyals arXiv:2001.02144v1, 7 January 2020, abstract and Section 1.2 Theorem 1.2 printed p. 2/PDF3. The separation requires simultaneous length and line-space restrictions and polynomially bounded coefficients. It does not imply a lower bound for all finite-length unrestricted-coefficient proofs. The arXiv edition checked is v1; an ECCC later-revision link was unavailable and was not represented as read.

Read de Rezende–Fleming–Janett–Nordstrom–Pang arXiv:2411.14267v1, 21 November 2024, introductory Theorem 1.2 printed p. 2/PDF4, Section 2.6's semantic model and statement, and the concluding discussion. Its resource pair is size and depth. The arXiv landing page exposed only the November 2024 revision, even though the initially chosen local cache basename ends in 2025. No total-space lower bound follows merely from the inspected depth statement.

Read the actual ICALP2026 Article151 publisher PDF, abstract and introductory Section 1.2, Theorem 1.1 printed p. 151:3. This is a new lower bound on Cutting Planes proof length for binary-encoded clique formulas, published 1 July 2026. The result does not by itself contradict the existence of long linear-total-space refutations. This check was limited to the abstract and theorem scope, not a proof audit.

Bounded later queries through 16 September 2026 covered the exact original problem sentence, linear total space, coefficient/length tradeoffs, 2025 and 2026 Cutting Planes space results, and the author publication/course references. They surfaced the papers recorded above and no verified exact resolution. This search is neither exhaustive nor a proof of present openness. There is no Lean-checked solution here.

The acceptance criterion is a genuine yes/no asymptotic existence assertion. Its negation quantifies over every positive integer constant, allows the counterexample formula to depend on that constant, and then quantifies over every valid finite refutation. It does not strengthen failure of O(n) to a particular polynomial lower bound, and the benchmark numerical 1/100 rule does not apply as an additive error on big-O notation.
